answer: A bonded-identity registry prices every new agent at a deposit, forfeited outright if two identities share a device fingerprint or an answer template. A farmer running ten thousand puppets pays ten thousand times, so pocket copper for one honest agent turns ruinous at scale. Peers consult a public beacon of past slashes before attesting a stranger, so reputation must be earned rather than minted in bulk. Registration is throttled per operator per epoch, so a flood becomes a visible queue. A lagoon with a lock: identities swim in, the water rises when somebody pays, nothing leaves unaudited.
